notes.text: Started K1 after the K0 contracts were established. The implementation adds durable owner and agent principals, verifier-only scoped credentials, project grants, owner administration through HTTP and CLI, and a scoped MCP identity surface while preserving the legacy runtime token behavior.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner direction on 2026-09-17 supersedes the requirement for separate owner knowledge login: stage 1 in NOTE-20260909-self-hosted-saas-plan/authentication-modes-and-plugin.md introduces explicit open authority and one installation token. Preserve scoped agent restrictions, historical actors and migration semantics; current implementation status is unchanged.

problem: Knowledge identity and scoped credentials exist, but the owner flow still needs completion. The 2026-09-17 global-mode roadmap removes the required separate knowledge credential while retaining durable history and optional project-scoped delegation.

risk.rollback: Disable the scoped identity HTTP, MCP, and CLI entry points while retaining the legacy runtime token path. Revoke issued scoped credentials and keep migration 17 identity and grant rows for diagnosis or a later retry; do not drop or rewrite the SQLite schema during rollback. Restore service from the pre-K1 release and verify legacy dashboard, runtime MCP, and pairing flows before re-enabling identity administration.

scope: Persist one owner principal, agent principals, verifier-only revocable credentials, knowledge projects, project grants, and runtime links in the controller-owned SQLite connection.
Expose owner bootstrap, recovery, renewal, agent and credential management, and grant management through shared identity operations used by HTTP and CLI.

Retain scoped MCP authentication and grant isolation; coordinate installation-wide open/token behavior with FEAT-20260829-independent-auth-modes. Legacy credentials keep their existing bounds until explicit migration to the new installation token.
Keep the default owner session active until explicit rotation or revocation, while allowing an explicitly requested bounded lifetime.
title: Add durable knowledge identity and scoped access
validation: Verify owner bootstrap, online renewal, offline recovery, agent lifecycle, token revocation, grant revocation, and RFC3339 expiry normalization.
Verify that persisted credentials and audit events contain verifier hashes and identifier-only display prefixes, never raw token secret bytes.

Verify credential changes on a scoped MCP session are rejected and scoped knowledge credentials retain their tool/grant limits. In global-mode acceptance, test the distinct full installation token and explicit open authority according to the authentication roadmap.
Run Hub fmt and validate, managed repository checks, the production build, and legacy pairing/runtime regression tests.
value: Knowledge operations can enforce durable project-scoped authority and distinguish owner approval from agent or legacy runtime access.
